title: It Has to Keep Coming
logline: Fifteen kilometres north of a dry-zone town, a three-kilometre earth bank holds back a stream that only runs in the wet months, and out of that water one line runs in one direction to about ninety thousand people: an intake, a buried main, an aerator, a clarifier, filter beds, chlorine, a pump house and three towers, with nowhere along it more than a few hours of water standing still.
human_question: If a thing goes on only because something keeps arriving, what exactly is it that is going on?

place.what_kind_of_place: Flat dry-zone country in the far north of the island's interior: scrub forest, paddy in the low ground, home gardens, and a stream that runs hard for a few months of the year and is a bed of sand for the rest. Across that stream, fifteen kilometres north of the town it serves, stands an earth bank three kilometres long and five metres wide with a radial-gate spillway in it, built for one purpose only, to hold drinking water, and not to irrigate anything. Behind it lies a sheet of water of about two hundred and fifty hectares at full supply. Immediately below the bank is a works: an intake, sixteen hundred metres of four-hundred-millimetre ductile iron buried alongside an unpaved road, an aerator, an upflow clarifier with a hydraulic flocculator, rapid filters, a chlorinator, a sludge thickener and open drying beds, the whole of it in square concrete tanks about twenty metres a side and ten metres deep that stand half above the ground and half below it, and a masonry pump house with four pumps rated at three thousand cubic metres a day each. Then fifteen and a half kilometres of buried main to a ground tank at the town's north-western edge, four pump stations, some forty kilometres of pumping main, and three elevated reservoirs: one of fifteen hundred cubic metres and one of a thousand, both new, and an older one of six hundred and seventy-five in the middle of the town. Off to one side, three kilometres south-east of the town, a well-field of boreholes twenty metres deep, whose harder water is blended into the treated surface water at one of the towers. And at the end of all of it the town: low, dusty, strung along a highway, the most southerly large town of a region that is largely forest, about ninety thousand people by design.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because the argument is the geometry, and the geometry is visible in a single move from the air. Lift off the water behind the bank at first light and the film's whole subject is in one frame: a sheet of water in grey scrub, an earth bank, a works below it, a line of buried pipe running away under a road, and on the horizon the towers of the town that the water is for. Every stage in that line takes what the stage before produced and gives it nothing back. Nothing in it is reciprocal and nothing in it is a web. And the reserve is thin in a way you can film: the towers between them hold hours, not weeks, so the town is always living inside a short lag between what has arrived and what is being drawn. Close up, the place is all thresholds: a gauge board with the water standing well below the marks somebody painted for it, a weir plate with a sheet of water going over it, sludge lifting off the floor of a clarifier, a filter bed boiling during a backwash, a float switch in a tower, a valve turned at six in the morning. The most beautiful thing here and the clearest statement of the concept are the same shot.
place.what_moves_or_changes: The water level against the bank, which falls all through the dry months and is the only number anybody here really watches. The colour of the raw water, which is clear and low for weeks and then turns to milky brown within an hour of the first storm, so that the plant has to be rebalanced around it. The sludge blanket in the clarifier. The filters, which are taken out one at a time and backwashed. The towers, which fill through the night and drop through the morning. The hours of supply, which are shifted between zones when the plant cannot keep up. And once a year the supply itself stops arriving: the stream ends, and everything downstream of the bank goes on running out of what is already behind it.
place.when_it_looks_best: Two windows, and the film wants both. The last weeks of the long dry spell, when the water is at its lowest, the bed is showing, the works are running hardest and the arithmetic is tightest; and the first storms of the north-east monsoon, when the stream arrives all at once, the raw water turns and the spillway has something to do. Within a day, the hour after first light, when the towers are full, the town starts drawing and the works are already making the next day's water; and the last half hour of light on a tower over flat roofs. The plant has no season indoors and wants a full week rather than a day, because the point is repetition.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A complete and quiet film about where a town's water comes from, which almost nobody has seen. A sheet of water in scrub behind a bank somebody built for it. Concrete rooms half underground with water moving through them in a fixed order. Air being blown through water. Floc forming and settling. A filter bed lifting and boiling. The smell of chlorine. A pump house at night. Fifteen kilometres of pipe you can only see as a scar in the road. A tower standing over a flat town at dusk, and a tap. It has its own shape with nothing said over it: arrival, treatment, carriage, storage, use, and the hour when the stream stops coming.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same hour becomes the sources' account of nutriment: support given by something that has to keep arriving, as against support given by a single push. The texts count four such supports and are exact that the first of them, food, is what keeps a body's matter going long after whatever started it, and that a being which stops receiving it weakens and dies. Laid over a waterworks this stops being a figure of speech: the town is not connected to the water, it is being delivered, continuously, in one direction, at a rate. And the film uses the same sources to refuse the warm reading its own group invites. The texts do not say everything is connected. They say which thing supports which, in which of twenty-four named ways, and they list what each kind of support does not reach. The voice says that out loud, because a pipeline is the plainest possible refutation of a web.

sequence.on_screen: First light, high, looking north. A sheet of still water in grey scrub, an earth bank drawn across it in a long shallow curve, and below the bank a small grid of pale concrete tanks. Far off at the bottom of frame, a flat town with two towers standing over it.
sequence.voice: None of the water in that town is from that town. It is here first, behind a bank three kilometres long that was built to hold drinking water and nothing else, and it gets there along one line, in one direction, all day.

sequence.on_screen: Ground level at the bank. A gauge board with the water standing a long way below the painted marks. Then the intake, and the line of a buried main running away under an unpaved road, visible only as a seam in the surface.
sequence.voice: The old analysis of cause does not offer one idea of cause at all. It offers a question: in what way, exactly, does this help? The commentary's own example is a matchbox. The chemical on the match and the chemical on the box both help make the flame, in different ways, and if they helped in the same way one of them would have been enough [C082-M:L3–L5]. Nothing that arises, it says, arises from a single condition, and the same thing can help one thing as a root and another as an object or a background [C082-P:L97].

sequence.on_screen: Inside the works. Air driven up through water in the aerator. Floc forming in the clarifier and drifting down. A rapid filter taken out of service and backwashed, the bed lifting and boiling. Chlorine dosing. Nothing human in frame for a long time.
sequence.voice: One of the twenty-four named supports is called nutriment, and it means exactly this: help given by something that has to keep arriving, rather than help given once. The texts count four of them, and the first is the nutritive essence of what is eaten and drunk [C075-P:L413–L416; C075-M:L126]. That one, they say, keeps up and grows the matter of a body that something else began, and a being who stops receiving it grows weak and dies [C075-P:L418–L424].

sequence.on_screen: A pump house at night: four pumps, gauges, a man writing a figure on a board. Then a tower filling in the dark, and at dawn the same tower's level dropping as the town starts to draw.
sequence.voice: The commentary's own picture for this is a rice seedling. The strength in the seed is what chiefly makes the plant come up; water and manure are what chiefly keep it alive and growing for months afterwards [C075-M:L130]. Which is to say the thing that started something and the thing that is keeping it going are not the same thing, and the second one has to turn up again today. These towers hold hours. Not weeks. Hours.

sequence.on_screen: The well-field south-east of the town: a borehole head, a meter, hard water running clear. Then the point at a tower where that water and the treated surface water are mixed, and a single outlet beyond it.
sequence.voice: Two supplies of different quality, arriving by different routes, making one thing that neither of them would have made alone. The sources are firm that support is not one relation but a list, and that what a given kind of support does not reach has to be named as carefully as what it does [C082-P:L101].

sequence.on_screen: A long lateral aerial following the buried main from the works towards the town: a scar in an unpaved road, then a metalled road, then houses. Nothing coming back the other way.
sequence.voice: Here is the correction this film exists for. The same texts that describe all this are not describing a warm mutual belonging. Mutual support, where two things hold each other up at the same moment, is one item on the list, and the commentary says plainly that not everything which arises together supports back: matter produced by the mind does not return the favour [C082-P:L3346], and derived matter does not support other derived matter [C082-P:L3616–L3620]. Nothing in this pipe is reciprocal. It is ordered, and it runs one way.

sequence.on_screen: The dry bed of the stream above the impoundment: sand, cracked mud, cattle tracks, a road bridge over nothing. Then the water behind the bank, lower than in the first shot, with the old shoreline showing as a pale band.
sequence.voice: The other three nutriments are not food. One is contact: the texts say the world striking the six doors is what brings feeling, and that beings, enjoying the taste of it, do not grow weary of the round of births [C075-P:L426–L430]. Their image is a bird without a beak, which cannot eat and dies [C075-M:L132]. Notice what that is not. It is not advice to feed yourself good experiences. It is an account of what keeps the round going, written by people whose aim was its ending.

sequence.on_screen: Last light. The tower over the town. A standpipe, a hand, water. Then back at height: the bank, the works, the line, the town, going dark. No commentary over the final half minute.
sequence.voice: One more thing the sources are careful about, and it is the reason a film can be made out of a waterworks without it becoming a figure for a person. Support by presence is defined as help given by a thing simply existing while it exists, and the texts count seven kinds of it and then say outright that the unconditioned is not one of them [C082-P:L8230–L8234; C082-P:L8246]. Food supports a body by being present; the life faculty supports what it governs by being present [C082-P:L8644–L8652]. There is no line anywhere in the list for the one who owns any of it. The commentary says the faculties were taught precisely to get people out of the belief that something inside is doing the work [C075-M:L91].

concept_merge.why_together: C082 is the whole method and C075 supplies the one item in it that this place demonstrates without arrangement. C082 defines a condition as whatever helps unarisen mind, mental factors and matter to arise, to continue in succession and to grow, and holds that there is no phenomenon which is not a condition for something [C082-P:L91], while only mind, mental factors and matter are themselves conditioned [C082-P:L93–L95; C082-M:L7]. It insists nothing arises from one condition and that one thing helps different things in different ways [C082-P:L97], gives the matchbox as its picture of that [C082-M:L3–L5], and adds a third category nobody expects, the states a given condition does not reach, so that each kind of support is stated as three sets rather than one [C082-P:L101]. Inside that method it defines nutriment as the support that sustains the continuity of mind and matter over a long time [C082-P:L6843–L6850], names the four, says what each produces [C082-P:L6852–L6860], and makes the hard version of the claim: the continuity of kamma-born matter must receive the help of weather and of food, and if it does not the being dies [C082-P:L6866]. C075's compendium covers the same four nutriments from the other end, as one of seven lists of things that do work for the states arising with them: nutriment is a cause that especially brings about the arising and the continuance of mind and matter in one continuity [C075-M:L128; C075-P:L411], the first is the nutritive essence of food and its absence is death [C075-P:L418–L424], and the commentary's rice seedling separates what begins a thing from what keeps it [C075-M:L130]. A town's water supply puts those two statements into one landscape. It is a whole settlement of ninety thousand people sustained by a delivery that has to be made again every hour, along a line whose reserve is measured in hours, out of a stream that stops arriving every year.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That 'connected' is the wrong word and 'delivered' is the right one. Stated flat, nutriment sounds like a synonym for cause; filmed as a bank, a works, a main and a tower it becomes a rate, a direction and a lag, and the difference between what started something and what is holding it up becomes a thing you can watch a man write on a board at two in the morning. The pairing also lets the film carry the group's own correction rather than its slogan: C082 supplies, in as many words, the limit that mutual support is one relation among many and that much of what arises together does not support back [C082-P:L3346], so the one-way pipe is not a sad exception to a web but the ordinary case. What was dropped to get here matters as much as what was kept. The previous version of this idea filmed a family cooking for two days to welcome somebody home and then the leftovers, and read the object condition off their different memories of it: a private household occasion, filmed for the feelings it produced, with nutriment stretched to cover a meal. This version keeps C075's real content, support by what must keep arriving in its bounded sense, and takes the household out of the film entirely.

concept_links.why: The film is the digest's method and three of its twenty-four conditions, and nothing else. The method is stated on screen: the question is not what caused this but in what way this helps, with the matchbox as the source's own illustration [C082-M:L3–L5], with nothing arising from a single condition and one thing helping in several modes [C082-P:L97], and with the three sets including the excluded states [C082-P:L101]. The nutriment condition is the film's spine: the four nutriments and what each sustains [C082-P:L6843–L6850; C082-P:L6852–L6860], the first material and the other three immaterial [C082-P:L6862–L6864], and the blunt clause that a body's matter needs the continuing help of weather and food or the being dies [C082-P:L6866]. The presence condition gives the towers and the standing plant: help given by a thing existing while it exists, in seven kinds, with food and the life faculty as two of them, and with the explicit statement that the unconditioned is not a presence condition [C082-P:L8230–L8234; C082-P:L8236–L8244; C082-P:L8246; C082-P:L8644–L8652]. The mutuality material is used for its limit rather than its warmth, which is the whole reason this idea exists in this group: the leaning image is one relation, and the text says not everything arising together supports back [C082-P:L3346], and that derived matter does not support other derived matter [C082-P:L3616–L3620]. Every limit in the digest that bears on this film is honoured. 'Everything is connected' is refused on screen in the sixth beat, in the digest's own terms. The film is not offered as ecology, as a social network or as physical causation, and the matchbox is spoken as an analogy in the source rather than as the doctrine. Presence is never turned into 'just being there is a gift'; the digest's own counter-example, that delighting in the eye by its presence gives rise to lust [C082-P:L8712–L8722], is the reason the voice keeps presence technical. The absence condition is not borrowed as 'letting go makes room', and is not used at all here. Predominance, repetition, the kamma and result conditions, the supernormal-knowledge examples, the passages on the gravest acts and on fixed wrong view, and the material on revering one's own merit [C082-P:L1723–L1727] are all unused. No claim is made anywhere that anybody's supply, shortage or circumstances are deserved.

The digest's fourth list, and only that. Nutriment is defined there as a cause that especially brings about the arising and the continuance of the mind and matter of one continuity [C075-M:L128; C075-P:L411]; the four are named [C075-P:L413–L416; C075-M:L126]; the first is the nutritive essence of what is eaten and drunk, which produces food-born matter and sustains the continuity and growth of the other kinds, so that a being who receives none weakens and dies [C075-P:L418–L424]; the rice-seedling simile separates the seed's strength, which brings the plant up, from the water and manure, which keep it alive for months [C075-M:L130]; contact brings feeling at the six doors and, being enjoyed, keeps beings from wearying of the round [C075-P:L426–L430], with the bird's beak as the source's image [C075-M:L132]; and the fourth nutriment, consciousness, brings mind and matter with it [C075-P:L434–L438], with the first counted as material and the other three as immaterial [C075-M:L138]. The closing beat uses the digest's own reason for teaching the faculties, which is to free people from the idea that something inside is doing the work [C075-M:L91]. The digest's limits are kept, and two of them are load-bearing here. Nutriment is not allowed to become a wellness slogan about feeding people or feeding a mind: the voice says in the seventh beat that these are called nutriments because they keep the round going and that the aim of the account is its ending. And the digest's sharpest warning is obeyed by omission: the commentary's tree simile, which ties good roots in a past life to wealth and honour and says a person of weak merit may live as a servant with barely enough to eat, is nowhere in this film, is not paraphrased, and could not be, because no household, income, tap or shortage is on screen as anybody's condition. The mixed-list material on roots, absorption factors, path factors, powers and dominants is unused, the sex-faculty passages and the Margaya's claim about men's and women's thoughts are unused, and the eight-root rebirth of great beings is unused.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That the texts distinguish between what starts something and what keeps it going, that they have a specific name for the second kind of help, meaning support by something that must keep arriving, and that a body is held up that way by food and weather so plainly that its interruption is death. And that this is not the cheerful claim that everything is connected: the sources describe ordered, named, mostly one-way supports, and say what each of them does not reach. Nothing is claimed about anybody's water, household or circumstances.
what_must_be_real: The scheme as it actually runs, including whatever is broken, silted, under-supplied, out of service or rationed in the week the crew is there. No tank, tower, gauge or valve is cleaned, repainted, re-lit or operated for the camera, and no reading is repeated for a second take. The film does not go into anybody's house: no tap, bill, connection, meter, queue, complaint or water-buying arrangement belonging to a named household appears, and no person is asked to describe going without. Operators are filmed as people doing work, are not made into characters, and are not asked to confirm any doctrine. Nothing is filmed that would compromise the security of a public water supply, and any sludge, discharge or water-quality problem that is visible is shown as it is rather than avoided or dramatised.
position_hint: early to middle in the group: it is the plainest statement of what kind of help the group is actually about, and it does the group's correcting work before the later films rely on it, since it says out loud that the sources describe ordered one-way support and not a web. It hands on the question of what happens when the supply tightens rather than stops. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: The group's own title. A film about a pipeline can slide into 'everything is connected', which is the one reading the sources refuse; the sixth beat exists to stop it and must not be cut.
Letting the waterworks become a figure for a body, so that the film quietly says 'you are a system like this', which the digest's limits do not support and which the series' floor forbids.
Turning nutriment into wellness: feeding a town, feeding a mind, feeding a soul.

The scheme's affordability and connection-fee arguments are real and public. Filming the plant beautifully while ignoring them is a posture; filming them is a different film. The line the voice holds is that this one is about the rate and direction of delivery, not about who can pay.
Any implication that a household with less water has less coming to it for a reason. The digest's tree simile is the exact form that error takes, and it is why no household is in the film.
Poverty or drought as spectacle: cracked mud, dust and a dry riverbed are photogenic and can quietly become an image of desert rather than of a dry season.
Borrowing the presence condition as an emotional idea about showing up for people.
Making an institution's routine look like a vigil, or its operators look like guardians of a mystery.
Filming infrastructure in a region where infrastructure is politically charged, and appearing to take a side in whose project it is.
drop_if: The water authority will not permit the impoundment, the works and the towers to be filmed, since the film is those three things and the line between them.
No dry-season low water and no first-storm turbidity fall inside the filming window, so the film's only two events would have to be narrated rather than seen.
Filming cannot be done without putting a household's supply, bill or shortage on screen.
Height cannot be obtained over the impoundment or the town at all, so the single shot the film is built on does not exist.
The only way to show the plant working is to have operations staged or re-run for the camera.

connections.note: Two places kept going by something that has to arrive again within the hour: one delivers water in one direction to a town, the other feeds a fire that has not been allowed to stop.
This one asks what it means to be supplied at all; the other asks what visibly changes when the same supply tightens.
Two films in the group on support that has to keep arriving rather than support given once; this one carries it on an institution and a pipe, with no household in it at all.

selection.reason: One aerial shot contains the concept: water, a bank, a works, a line and a town, in that order and in one direction. It is also the group's best chance to refuse 'everything is connected' with footage rather than with a caveat.

review.note: Rewritten 2026-09-24 into the footage-led shape, and the subject replaced. What was dropped: the entire old subject, a family cooking for two days to welcome somebody home and then the leftovers, with the concept read off the different things each member of the household later felt about it. It was dropped for three reasons. It filmed a private household occasion and depended on people being willing to say honest, mixed things about each other on camera; it made a household's feelings the illustration of a doctrine; and it hung the supporting concept on a stretched reading of nutriment, in which a meal stood for the sources' bounded term. The concepts were kept and re-grounded. C075 is now used only for what it actually says about nutriment, support by something that has to keep arriving, with the commentary's rice-seedling simile spoken as the source's own picture, and the digest's warning against the wellness reading answered out loud in the seventh beat. C082 is now the method itself plus the nutriment and presence conditions, and its mutuality material is used for its limit rather than its warmth, because the group's title invites exactly the reading the sources refuse. Both digests were re-read from scratch and every citation re-tested against digest evidence rather than carried over; the old file's uncited claims about the object condition are not reused anywhere. The film now contains no household, no private occasion and nobody's circumstances, and the one shot it is built on is a dawn aerial of an impoundment, a works and a town in a line.

suggested_location.name: The Per Aru drinking-water reservoir and the Vavuniya water treatment works, with the town's overhead reservoirs

also_known_as.name: Peru Aru
also_known_as.meaning: the same seasonal stream, spelled both ways in project documents and in the press

also_known_as.name: Puthunkulam reservoir
also_known_as.meaning: the reservoir named for the village at which the bund across the stream was built, about fifteen kilometres north of the town

also_known_as.name: overhead reservoir, OR
also_known_as.meaning: the local and trade term for an elevated water tower

suggested_location.region: Vavuniya District, Northern Province: the dry-zone scrub, paddy and home-garden country immediately north of the district town, on the A9 corridor, with the impoundment about fifteen kilometres north of the town and the distribution towers in and around it
suggested_location.why_here: Because this is the country's first large reservoir built for drinking water alone, so the place is not an irrigation landscape with a pipe attached: the whole point of the bank, the sheet of water behind it and the works below it is to deliver a town's daily supply, in one direction, at a rate. The stream it impounds is seasonal, which gives the film the one event that makes nutriment legible, an annual stop in arrival, without anyone having to arrange it. The engineering is unusually filmable and unusually sequential: an intake, sixteen hundred metres of buried main, an aerator, a clarifier, rapid filters, chlorination, sludge beds, a four-pump house, fifteen and a half kilometres of main, a ground tank, four pump stations and three towers, in that order and only that order. The towers hold hours, which is the film's central fact. The district is also among the thinnest on the slate, the site is a working public utility that can consent, there is no private grief anywhere in it, and nobody has to be an example of anything.
what_to_film: The impoundment and the bank from height at first light and last light, framed so that the works below the bank and the town's towers on the horizon are in the same shot.
The gauge board and the shoreline through the dry months, with the old waterline showing as a pale band above the water.
The intake and the buried raw-water main: the seam in the unpaved road, and the run of it towards the works.

The treatment sequence in order and without commentary: aeration, flocculation, the clarifier's floc forming and settling, a rapid filter taken out of service and backwashed, chlorine dosing, the sludge thickener and the open drying beds.
The concrete geometry of the tanks, which stand half above and half below the ground, in hard midday light from directly overhead.
The pump house at night: four pumps, gauges, a logbook, a figure written on a board.
A tower filling through the night and dropping through the morning, with the level and the float switch visible.
The well-field south-east of the town, and the point where its harder water is blended into the treated surface water.
The dry bed of the stream above the impoundment in the last weeks before the monsoon: sand, cracked mud, a road bridge over nothing.
The first storm: the stream arriving, the raw water turning brown within the hour, the spillway with something to do, and the plant being rebalanced around it.
suggested_location.access: By road north from the district town along the main highway for the impoundment and the works, and within the town for the ground tank and the towers. Everything depends on written permission from the national water authority, whose regional office is in the town, and the works is an operating public utility rather than a visitor site. The impoundment is a drinking-water source, so access to the bank, the intake and the water itself is likely to be restricted on public-health grounds as well as security ones. Flying anything over a water source and over infrastructure in this region is not to be assumed: clearance would have to be sought from the authority and from the police or military authorities who still hold parts of the area, and may be refused, in which case the elevated views have to come from the bank itself and from the towers. Dry-season access to the bed above the impoundment is by track and on foot.
suggested_location.best_time: The last weeks before the north-east monsoon, roughly September into October, for the lowest water and the hardest-working plant; the first storms, late October into November, for the arrival and the turbidity. Within a day, the hour after first light and the last half hour of light. A full working week rather than a day, because the film's subject is repetition, and a second short visit planned for whichever week the first storm actually breaks.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only and unverified on the ground. From the sources above: the scheme was designed under a dry-zone urban water and sanitation project, begun after 2009 and reported complete in 2019, serving about 80,000 people initially with 12,000 cubic metres a day and more than 14,000 service connections reported by 2025; an earth bund across the seasonal stream to the north of the town impounds a reservoir given variously as 215, 250.5 and 640 hectares in different sources, described in the press as the country's first large reservoir built solely for drinking water; the bund is described as 5 metres wide with a radial-gate spillway, and its length is given as 1.5 km in one project summary and 3 km in another; the treatment works stands immediately downstream of the bund and comprises an aerator, an upflow clarifier with hydraulic flocculator, rapid filters, a chlorinator and a sludge thickener in tanks of about 20 by 20 metres and 10 metres deep, set half above and half below ground, with a masonry pump house of four pumps of 3,000 cubic metres a day; a raw-water main of 1.6 km of 400 mm ductile iron runs from the intake to the works; a treated-water main of 15.5 km runs to a ground tank on the north-western edge of the town; the contractor's own record lists two new elevated towers of 1,500 and 1,000 cubic metres, sludge drying beds, a chlorination building, a generator house and SCADA; project documents name an existing 675 cubic metre tower in the town centre, six new boreholes at a well-field about 3 km south-east of the town whose water is blended with treated surface water at one of the towers, four pump stations and about 41 km of pumping main; and the divisional area is recorded as 38 per cent forested. The coordinate is a direction, not a survey: project documents place the bund at a village fifteen kilometres north of the town, while an online gazetteer gives a similarly named place only two or three kilometres from the town centre, which does not match that distance, so the figure given here is an approximate point fifteen kilometres north of the town on the stream and no dam, tank, tower or plot has been identified. Three things the film depends on are inferences rather than confirmed facts: that the works can be filmed internally at all, that the towers' storage is as thin in practice as the design figures suggest, and that low water and first-storm turbidity can both be caught in one season. Nobody has been approached and no permission has been sought from the water authority or any other body. No photograph of the reservoir, the works or any tower was found on Wikimedia Commons; the one image is of the town the scheme supplies.

unknowns: Whether the national water authority will open the impoundment, the treatment works and the towers to a crew, and who else has to agree in a region where some land and access remain under military or police control.

Whether height can be obtained over a drinking-water source and over the town at all, given both public-health restrictions and airspace control, or whether the film has to work from the bank and the towers.
